# HDropdownMenu

> A keyboard-operated command menu with a touch-friendly bottom panel on mobile.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.7.1. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HDropdownMenu` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-dropdown-menu>`.
- Constructor: `HearthDropdownMenuElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Controls.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HDropdownMenu.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- This is a command menu with menuitem roles; use HNavigationMenu for route navigation.
- Arrow keys, Home/End, typeahead, Escape, and Tab work with disabled commands excluded from focus navigation. select(id) requests an application action.
- mobileBreakpoint sets the mobile viewport threshold in CSS pixels. Per-component props override the inherited --h-mobile-breakpoint value from HTheme; the fallback is 640px. Set 0 to keep desktop presentation. The breakpoint updates live across Vue and custom-element shadow roots.

## Public API

items: MenuAction[] · label: string · icon: IconValue · open, disabled, iconOnly: boolean · placement: top | bottom | left | right · mobileBreakpoint: number (CSS px; inherited, 640 default; 0 disables)

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    items: MenuAction[];
    label?: string;
    icon?: IconValue;
    iconOnly?: boolean;
    open?: boolean;
    disabled?: boolean;
    placement?: "top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right";
    mobileBreakpoint?: number;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ items: () => [], label: "Actions", placement: "bottom" }
```

### Events

select(id), update:open(boolean)

```ts
type Emits = {
    select: [
        id: string
    ];
    "update:open": [
        open: boolean
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

icon, trigger-label

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, menu, item, header

Use `hearth-dropdown-menu::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export interface MenuAction {
    id: string;
    label: string;
    icon?: IconValue;
    shortcut?: string;
    disabled?: boolean;
    danger?: boolean;
    separatorBefore?: boolean;
}

export type IconValue = string | IconDefinition;

export interface IconDefinition {
    paths: readonly string[];
    viewBox?: string;
    fill?: "none" | "currentColor";
    fillRule?: "nonzero" | "evenodd";
    strokeWidth?: number;
}
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HDropdownMenu } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';
const actions = [{id:'edit',label:'Edit',icon:'settings'},{id:'remove',label:'Remove',danger:true,separatorBefore:true}];
function act(id: string) { /* Perform the selected application action. */ }
</script>

<template>
  <HDropdownMenu label="Application actions" :items="actions" @select="act" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-dropdown-menu');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Application actions",
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "edit",
      "label": "Edit",
      "icon": "settings"
    },
    {
      "id": "remove",
      "label": "Remove",
      "danger": true,
      "separatorBefore": true
    }
  ]
});

element.addEventListener('select', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
